messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High latency detected in dedicated pool (Pelorus) - p95 > 20s in us-west-2. Paging matt_oncall for investigation.

matt_oncall: paging — I’m on it. pulling logs and checking node health.

sara_runtime: seeing KV cache thrashing for tenant pelorus-tenant-42. spikes align with large batch jobs from that tenant.

liam_sre: confirmed noisy tenant. memory pressure on node g4-xx-12, OOM margins low. starting isolation plan.

matt_oncall: taking tenant offline (drain) and routing affected traffic to hosted fallback for now. initiating graceful offload.

ops-bot: runbook action executed: cordon-tenant pelorus-tenant-42 by matt_oncall.

matt_oncall: cordoned. starting graceful offload + edge throttling for 60s then migrate. will report back in 5.

omar_se: I notified Pelorus SRE on the support channel — told them to expect degraded latencies and a brief spike in errors during migration. @nina_csm, please prep customer-facing note.

nina_csm: DM'd account lead and legal. Drafting exec note to share once we confirm impact window. :writing_hand:

sara_runtime: applied KV TTL bump and dropped batch size to 1 for the tenant. should reduce cache churn. quick logs below:
```
[2024-11-02T03:12:44Z] tenant=pelorus-tenant-42 kv_misses=12452 qps=4200 mem=92%
```

liam_sre: nodes rebalanced. non-impacted tenants p95 improved (18s -> 300ms). Pelorus tenant still at ~1.2s during migration.

matt_oncall: switching mitigation to fallback routing now. marking incident as customer-impacting and creating post-incident channel.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-20241102-0912. Severity: sev2. Night handoff scheduled at 2024-11-02T04:00Z.

kelly_prod: proposed copy for customer comm: "We detected sustained latency for your dedicated pool and isolated the noisy tenant; we routed traffic to a fallback to preserve availability. We're calculating impact and credits and will follow up with a timeline." Thoughts?

nina_csm: looks good. please add the affected UTC window and a named contact for follow-up (me).

omar_se: suggest we offer a temporary dedicated bump or pin their critical traffic to quieter hosts while RCA is finalized.

matt_oncall: agree. will keep a small pinned pool for them for 24h and open a capacity ticket for immediate bump.

sara_runtime: created RCA draft in gdoc (placeholder link) — initial hypothesis: KV cache storm from long-prefix batching caused OOM thrash on g4 nodes for that tenant.

liam_sre: adding evidence: core dumps and GC logs attached to ticket #4567. autoscaler failed to scale because cluster reached quota — needs follow-up.

nina_csm: customer update 1 scheduled for 2024-11-02T05:00Z. I'll send the exec brief after your sign-off, @matt_oncall.

matt_oncall: handing off active watch to night_oncall (jordan_oncall). escalate if p95 > 5s or error rate >2%. TL;DR in incident doc.

jordan_oncall: acknowledged. will monitor metrics and comment in the doc. ping if it regresses.

kelly_prod: post-incident deliverables: SLA credit calc, exec one-pager, and a technical call with Pelorus engineering. assigning owners now.

nina_csm: I will own the exec one-pager and customer comm. @omar_se to run the tech call. @liam_sre will lead RCA timeline and coordinate credits calc with finance.

matt_oncall: closing active mitigation — systems stable. last check p95 = 320ms across pool. marking incident as mitigated at 2024-11-02T05:20Z. preparing final RCA and credit calc.

ops-bot: INC-20241102-0912 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owners assigned: nina_csm, liam_sre, omar_se. :white_check_mark: 

nina_csm: thanks team. I'll post the draft customer comm in #customer-success and link the RCA once the tech details are confirmed.
